query: Overall, our results unmask an active role of the proteinaceous TMD in membrane fusion that clearly goes beyond simple membrane anchoring and may be used to optimize release from differentially sized vesicles. ß-branched amino acids are key determinants for the fusogenic role of the v-SNARE TMD, most likely promoting the conformational dynamics of the TMD helix, which may perturb the packing of the surrounding phospholipids and thereby facilitate first intermembrane contact as well as fusion pore expansion.
